cds.text: Recognise that sentences are key units for expressing ideas
Understand that a simple sentence has a single independent clause representing one event or idea
Understand that compound sentences link two or more independent clauses, usually with a coordinating conjunction, to connect ideas
Recognise that sentences are groups of words working together to make meaning
Understand word classes: nouns (including pronouns), verbs, adjectives and adverbs, and what each represents
Understand that nouns can extend into noun groups with articles and adjectives, and verbs can form verb groups
Identify punctuation as a feature of written text that differs from letters; capitals mark names and sentence starts; punctuation marks sentence ends
Understand full stops, question marks and exclamation marks, and capitals for familiar proper nouns
Recognise capitals in titles and commas separating items in lists
Recognise and generate rhyming words, alliteration, syllables and phonemes in spoken words (phonological awareness)
Segment words into separate phonemes, including consonant blends or clusters at the beginning and end of words
Manipulate more complex sounds in spoken words, using blending, segmenting, phoneme deletion and substitution to read and write words
Segment sentences into words; blend and segment single-syllable words; isolate, blend and manipulate phonemes
Orally manipulate initial, medial and final phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution to generate new words
Recognise and name upper- and lower-case letters and know the most common sound each letter represents
Read one- and two-syllable words
Use short and common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs to write and blend words; read consonant clusters and silent letters in words of one or more syllables, including compound words
Write CVC words by representing sounds with letters, and blend sounds when reading CVC words
Understand that a letter can represent more than one sound and that every syllable must contain a vowel sound
Use knowledge of letters and sounds to spell words
Spell one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns
Use spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words not fully predictable from sounds, including high-frequency words
Read and write some high-frequency and familiar words
Read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words
Build morphemic word families using knowledge of prefixes and suffixes
Understand that words are units of meaning and can be made of more than one meaningful part
Recognise and use grammatical morphemes to create word families

sentences.text: {{S}} applies correct letter patterns and general rules when spelling words.
{{S}} applies correct spelling patterns and general rules when writing.
{{S}} has shown improvement in spelling by identifying letter patterns to support correct spelling.
{{S}} applies common letter patterns and general rules when spelling and continues to develop accuracy.
{{S}} applies some spelling patterns and general rules when writing.
{{S}} applies familiar spelling patterns and is working towards greater accuracy when spelling less common words.
{{S}} spells familiar words by using common letter patterns and recognising the sounds in words.
{{S}} spells words with double letters and identifies the meaning of most words by recognising their spelling.
{{S}} spells simple words with common endings and uses basic strategies to spell unfamiliar words with some success.
{{S}} is learning to apply common spelling patterns in writing.
{{S}} constructs sentences that include basic punctuation and is learning to use capital letters and full stops correctly.
{{S}} is beginning to identify nouns and verbs in simple sentences.
{{S}} spells common words correctly and sounds out unfamiliar words with care.
{{S}} writes {{pos}} first name by putting the letters in the right order.
{{S}} writes short sentences using familiar language and is improving {{pos}} use of full stops.
{{S}} adds 's' to words to show more than one, such as changing 'cat' to 'cats'.
{{S}} writes related sentences to create stories and adds phrases that show time and place.
{{S}} breaks words into sounds as a spelling strategy.
{{S}} spells high-frequency words correctly in {{pos}} writing.
{{S}} breaks longer words into chunks as a strategy for spelling.
{{S}} spells words with prefixes, such as un- and re-.
{{S}} spells words with suffixes, such as -ful and -est.
{{S}} recognises common word beginnings such as 'un-' and 're-', and correctly uses them when spelling.
{{S}} checks {{pos}} work for spelling mistakes and uses dictionaries to correct them.
{{S}} uses commas to separate parts of a sentence and apostrophes for contractions.
{{S}} varies sentence length to improve {{pos}} writing.
{{S}} matches the letters in {{pos}} name and puts them in the correct order.
{{S}} recognises words that start with the same sound.
{{S}} identifies letters in familiar words.

rows.newText: {{S}} knows that a sentence is a group of words that work together to share an idea.
{{S}} uses capital letters and full stops to mark the start and end of a sentence.
{{S}} claps syllables and recognises words that rhyme or start with the same sound.
{{S}} writes simple consonant-vowel-consonant words by matching sounds to letters.
{{S}} blends sounds to read simple consonant-vowel-consonant words.
{{S}} uses letter and sound knowledge to spell simple words.
{{S}} reads and writes familiar words such as I, the and is.
{{S}} knows that some words, such as compound words, can be made of more than one meaningful part.
{{S}} writes a simple sentence that tells about one event or idea.
{{S}} writes complete simple sentences that make sense.
{{S}} uses nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs when writing sentences.
{{S}} ends sentences with full stops, question marks or exclamation marks and uses capitals for names.
{{S}} breaks words into separate sounds, including blends, to help with reading and spelling.
{{S}} separates the first, middle and last sounds of words and changes them to make new words.
{{S}} reads one- and two-syllable words with growing confidence.
{{S}} knows that a letter can stand for more than one sound and that every syllable has a vowel.
{{S}} spells one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns.
{{S}} reads and writes an increasing number of common words correctly.
{{S}} adds endings such as -s, -ed and -ing to words to change their meaning.
{{S}} writes compound sentences by joining ideas with words such as and, but and so.
{{S}} uses linking words to join two ideas into one sentence.
{{S}} extends nouns into noun groups using articles and adjectives.
{{S}} uses capitals in titles and commas in lists.
{{S}} uses commas to separate items in a list and capital letters in titles.
{{S}} blends and segments complex sounds in spoken words.
{{S}} swaps, adds and removes sounds in spoken words to make new words.
{{S}} uses short and long vowels, blends and digraphs to read and write words.
{{S}} uses spelling patterns and word parts to spell words that cannot be sounded out.
{{S}} builds word families using prefixes and suffixes.
{{S}} knows that sentences are made of words and that a sentence tells a complete idea.
{{S}} puts words in order to make a sentence that makes sense.
{{S}} breaks words into sounds, including blends, then uses them to read and spell.
{{S}} changes, adds or removes sounds in spoken words to make new words.
{{S}} reads one-syllable and two-syllable words by blending the parts.
